title: $p^*$ is braided
statement:
By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit] and [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-tensor],
$p^*$ is strong monoidal. It is moreover braided: under the tensor comparison
isomorphisms, $p^*$ of the symmetry $F\otimes G\cong G\otimes F$ is the
symmetry $p^*F\otimes p^*G\cong p^*G\otimes p^*F$.

proof.text: Put $L=p^*$ and $R=p_*$, with $L\dashv R$ as in [def-sfb-point-adjunction], for the monoidal categories of abelian sheaves in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit], $L$ has its adjunction-induced oplax structure and its unit comparison $\iota:L\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$ is invertible. By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-tensor], all its tensor comparisons $\delta_{F,G}:L(F\otimes G)\to LF\otimes LG$ are invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-strong-monoidal-of-invertible-oplax] to this oplax structure. It supplies strong monoidal coherence with lax unit $j=\iota^{-1}$ and tensor maps $m_{F,G}=\delta_{F,G}^{-1}$, and retains the given oplax comparisons. Thus the associativity and both unit arguments formerly inline are precisely the cited promotion theorem.

proof.text: We check the braiding identity for the canonical lax tensor map $\mu_{A,B}:RA\otimes RB\to R(A\otimes B)$, for arbitrary abelian sheaves $A,B$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. By [def-sfb-point-lower-star], restriction evaluates at $u(S)=\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$. Before sheafification on the profinite site, $\mu_{A,B}$ is the natural presheaf map whose component at $S$ is $A(uS)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B(uS)\to(A\otimes B)(uS)$, the component of the sheafification unit for the objectwise tensor product. The target $R(A\otimes B)$ is a sheaf. Thus [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends this map uniquely to $RA\otimes RB$. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] and the explicit construction in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], the symmetry on sheaves is induced from the objectwise symmetry, and sheafification preserves it. Precompose the two maps $R(\beta_{A,B})\circ\mu_{A,B}$ and $\mu_{B,A}\circ\beta_{RA,RB}$ with the source sheafification unit. At each $S$, both send $a\otimes b$ to the image of $b\otimes a$ in $(B\otimes A)(uS)$. They therefore agree on the whole objectwise tensor product, and uniqueness in the sheafification universal property gives $R(\beta_{A,B})\circ\mu_{A,B}=\mu_{B,A}\circ\beta_{RA,RB}$. This proves the needed lax braided identity without asserting that restriction commutes with sheafification.

proof.text: Write $e:\operatorname{Id}\to RL$ for the adjunction unit and $\Phi_{H,K}:\operatorname{Hom}(LH,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,RK)$ for the adjunction bijection of [def-sfb-point-adjunction]. Its formula is $\Phi_{H,K}(h)=R(h)\circ e_H$. Unpacking the adjunction-induced oplax structure in [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit] gives $\Phi_{F\otimes G,LF\otimes LG}(\delta_{F,G})=\mu_{LF,LG}\circ(e_F\otimes e_G)$. This is the defining mate formula, rather than an additional compatibility theorem. For $f:H'\to H$ and $k:K\to K'$, the same formula and naturality of $e$ give $\Phi(k\circ h)=R(k)\circ\Phi(h)$ and $\Phi(h\circ L(f))=\Phi(h)\circ f$.

proof.text:
For condensed abelian groups $F,G$, compare maps $L(F\otimes G)\to LG\otimes LF$ under the bijection $\Phi$ of step 3. The lax braided identity of step 2, followed by naturality of the symmetry in the symmetric monoidal structures of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], gives the explicit calculation
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Phi(\beta_{LF,LG}\circ\delta_{F,G})
&=R(\beta_{LF,LG})\circ\mu_{LF,LG}\circ(e_F\otimes e_G)\\
&=\mu_{LG,LF}\circ\beta_{RLF,RLG}\circ(e_F\otimes e_G)\\
&=\mu_{LG,LF}\circ(e_G\otimes e_F)\circ\beta_{F,G}\\
&=\Phi(\delta_{G,F}\circ L(\beta_{F,G})).
\end{aligned}
$$
The last equality is the precomposition identity from step 3. Both sides have source $F\otimes G$ and target $R(LG\otimes LF)$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection [def-sfb-point-adjunction] yields $\beta_{LF,LG}\circ\delta_{F,G}=\delta_{G,F}\circ L(\beta_{F,G})$.

source.place: braided assertion; explicit expansion of the inherited proof sentence: compatibility is the mate under the adjunction

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-tensor], $\delta_{F,G}$ and $\delta_{G,F}$ are isomorphisms. Compose the identity of step 4 on the right with $\delta_{F,G}^{-1}$ and on the left with $\delta_{G,F}^{-1}$ to obtain
$$L(\beta_{F,G})\circ\delta_{F,G}^{-1}=\delta_{G,F}^{-1}\circ\beta_{LF,LG}.$$
This is exactly preservation of the symmetry by the strong monoidal structure from step 1. Together with the invertible unit comparison of [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-unit], it proves the whole statement.
